shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: The plant historically called Sophora secundiflora (Texas mountain laurel) is accepted as Dermatophyllum secundiflorum. DO NOT create a second species/genus-native record for Sophora in the local learner. The existing Dermatophyllum card has the useful traits: evergreen shrub/tree, alternate glossy pinnate leaves, purple hanging fragrant pea-flower clusters, thick woody pods and bright red hard seeds (HIGHLY TOXIC if ingested).
shared_genus_recognition.identity_warning: Source name refers to accepted Dermatophyllum; do not treat as second accepted plant

look_here_first_sequence: Recognize plant architecture and leaf arrangement before flower color.
Compare leaf shape, insertion and microstructures on several mature samples.
Inspect floral anatomy under magnification and track into mature fruit.
Cross-check the strongest lookalike with matched scale; avoid uncertain species IDs.
Respect the source-name/canonical manifest boundary and keep nonlocal native labels unchanged.
scientific_cautions: This is a redirected historical SOURCE name, NOT a treatment of genus Sophora globally; other accepted Sophora taxa exist but are not in this project pool.
Do not duplicate the installed Dermatophyllum secundiflorum species card, shift its accepted identity, or change its target-zone status.
The bright red seeds contain toxic alkaloids; do not ingest, encourage handling by children or taste-testing.
Existing Joey Santore media requires private-study-only handling unless rights cleared for public reuse.
